# Two-Wheeled Vehicle Frame

## Field of the Invention

The present invention concerns a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, such as a bicycle or motorcycle. The frame is constructed from two frame half-shells that are joined together to form a unified support frame. When assembled, these two half-shells create at least one inner cavity within the structure, resulting in a frame that combines structural strength with reduced overall weight.

## Structure of the Support Frame

The support frame is defined by at least one separating surface, which is the interface along which the two half-shells rest against one another. This separating surface establishes the plane at which the two components meet and are subsequently joined.

In addition to providing the primary structural body, the support frame preferably incorporates several integrated receiving areas designed to accommodate key components of the vehicle. These receiving areas are configured to hold a handlebar tube, a bottom bracket, and/or a seat tube. By integrating these mounting features directly into the half-shell construction, the frame simplifies assembly and enhances the overall rigidity of the finished vehicle.

## Rear Structure and Support Braces

At the rear of the frame, as viewed in the travel direction of the vehicle, the support frame forms a dedicated rear structure. This rear structure serves as the assembly point for mounting the rear wheel.

The rear structure comprises two distinct elements: a left-hand support brace and a right-hand support brace. These two braces are spaced apart from one another so that the rear wheel can be received and securely mounted in the space between them. This arrangement ensures proper alignment and stable support of the rear wheel during operation.

## Configuration of the Separating Surface

According to the invention, the separating surface does not merely divide the main body of the frame. Instead, it extends continuously between the two frame half-shells and, significantly, also runs through both the left-hand and the right-hand support braces.

This configuration means that each support brace is likewise formed from the two joined half-shells, following the same separating plane as the rest of the frame. As a result, the entire support frame—including the rear braces—can be manufactured as a consistent two-part shell construction, offering advantages in terms of production efficiency, structural uniformity, and weight reduction.

# Two-Wheeled Vehicle Frame Constructed from Joined Half-Shells

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, such as a bicycle, electric bicycle, or motorcycle. More specifically, it concerns a frame construction that is assembled from two joined half-shells, offering advantages in manufacturing simplicity, structural integration, and weight reduction.

## Background

Conventional two-wheeled vehicle frames are typically manufactured from multiple individual tubes or components that must be welded, bonded, or otherwise joined together in numerous separate operations. Such approaches require complex tooling, careful alignment of many parts, and multiple joining steps, all of which increase production time and cost. Furthermore, the rear structure that supports the rear wheel—often comprising separate stays and dropouts—adds additional components and assembly complexity to the overall frame.

There is therefore a need for a frame construction that reduces the number of components, simplifies assembly, and integrates the rear wheel mounting structure directly into the main frame body.

## Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a two-wheeled vehicle frame that is constructed from two joined half-shells. When brought together, these two half-shells form a support frame that encloses at least one inner cavity. This hollow construction contributes to a favorable strength-to-weight ratio while providing space that may be used, for example, to route cables or house additional components.

The support frame includes several receiving areas designed to accommodate the various functional components of the vehicle. These receiving areas include, among others, a region for mounting the handlebar assembly and a region for receiving the bottom bracket, which houses the pedal crank mechanism. By forming these mounting interfaces directly during the joining of the two half-shells, the frame integrates key attachment points without requiring separately added parts.

In addition to the main support frame, the construction includes a rear structure. This rear structure comprises a left support brace and a right support brace, which together serve to mount the rear wheel of the vehicle. The two braces extend rearward from the main body of the frame and provide the points at which the rear wheel axle is secured.

## Key Feature

The central feature of the invention lies in the arrangement of the separating surface between the two half-shells. This separating surface—that is, the plane or interface along which the two half-shells meet and are joined—runs not only between the two half-shells across the main body of the frame, but also continues through both the left and right support braces.

Because the separating surface passes directly through both support braces, the rear wheel mounting structure is formed as an integral part of the two-piece construction. Each half-shell thus contributes one portion of the main frame together with a corresponding portion of both rear braces. When the two half-shells are joined, the complete frame—including the fully formed rear structure—is created in a single, unified assembly.

## Advantages

This configuration enables a significantly simplified two-piece frame construction. Rather than assembling numerous individual tubes and separately attaching a rear wheel support assembly, the entire frame, including its rear wheel mounting structure, is produced from just two mating half-shells. This approach:

- Reduces the total number of components required;
- Simplifies the manufacturing and assembly process;
- Integrates the rear wheel mounting structure directly into the frame body;
- Allows for the formation of internal cavities that improve the strength-to-weight ratio; and
- Provides consistent, repeatable positioning of the component receiving areas.

In this way, the invention offers an efficient and structurally integrated solution for constructing two-wheeled vehicle frames.

# Patent Abstract

## Two-Wheeled Vehicle Frame Formed from Joined Half-Shells

A frame for a two-wheeled vehicle comprising two half-shells joined together to form an integral frame body defining an inner cavity therebetween. The half-shells are joined along a separating surface that extends substantially in a longitudinal median plane of the vehicle, such that each half-shell forms a laterally opposed portion of the frame. The separating surface may follow a contour extending between a steering head region at a forward end and a rear wheel region at a rearward end of the frame.

Each half-shell is formed as a substantially shell-shaped member having a peripheral edge, wherein the peripheral edges of the two half-shells are brought into abutment and connected along the separating surface to enclose the inner cavity. The resulting hollow construction provides high torsional and bending rigidity while reducing overall frame weight.

The frame further comprises rear wheel support braces integrally formed with or extending from the half-shells in the rear wheel region. The support braces are configured to extend rearwardly and to receive a rear wheel axle or a swing arm mounting therebetween. In one arrangement, each half-shell forms a respective one of the rear wheel support braces, the braces being spaced apart transversely to define a receiving space for the rear wheel.

The inner cavity formed between the joined half-shells may accommodate and enclose vehicle components, including fuel, electrical wiring, or other functional elements, thereby protecting such components and improving the compactness of the vehicle.

# Technical Summary: Two-Piece Shell Bicycle Frame

## Overview

The present invention relates to a bicycle frame constructed from two complementary shell halves that, when joined, form a hollow monocoque support structure. The frame integrates dedicated mounting interfaces for the handlebar assembly, bottom bracket, and seat tube.

## Structural Configuration

The frame comprises two shell halves—a first (e.g., left) shell and a second (e.g., right) shell—each formed as a substantially concave member. When mated along a joining plane, the two halves define an enclosed internal cavity, creating a lightweight yet rigid hollow support structure.

Each shell half is manufactured as a unitary piece, allowing the complex frame geometry (including the head tube region, top tube, down tube, seat tube region, and chain/seat stay areas) to be produced in a single forming operation per half.

## Joining Interface

The two shell halves are joined along mating edges to form a continuous seam. The joint may be secured by one or more of the following methods:

- **Adhesive bonding** along the mating flanges
- **Welding or fusion** (for metallic or thermoplastic materials)
- **Mechanical fastening** (e.g., internal ribs, tabs, or fasteners)
- **Co-molding or overlapping lap joints** for increased bond area

The joining plane may run generally along the vertical centerline of the frame (bilateral symmetry) to simplify tooling and ensure balanced load distribution.

## Integrated Mounting Areas

The joined structure incorporates three principal mounting interfaces, formed integrally within or reinforced at the shell halves:

1. **Handlebar/Steering Mount** — A head tube region at the forward portion of the frame, configured to receive a steerer tube, headset bearings, and the handlebar assembly.

2. **Bottom Bracket Mount** — A reinforced lower junction area configured to receive the bottom bracket shell, bearings, and crank spindle, positioned at the convergence of the down tube and lower frame members.

3. **Seat Tube Mount** — An upper rearward region configured to receive and support a seat post/seat tube assembly.

These mounting areas may include localized reinforcement, embedded inserts (e.g., metallic bushings or threaded fittings), or increased material thickness to accommodate concentrated loads and bearing interfaces.

## Materials and Manufacturing

The shell halves may be formed from:

- **Fiber-reinforced composite** (e.g., carbon fiber, glass fiber) via molding
- **Thermoplastic** via injection molding or thermoforming
- **Metal** (e.g., aluminum, magnesium) via stamping, hydroforming, or casting

Internal reinforcing ribs, webs, or bulkheads may be integrated into one or both shells to enhance stiffness, manage load paths, and support the mounting interfaces.

## Advantages

- **Reduced part count** and simplified assembly compared to multi-tube welded frames
- **Design flexibility** enabling complex, optimized geometries and aerodynamic profiles
- **Weight reduction** through hollow monocoque construction
- **Cost-effective mass production** using matched tooling
- **Integrated cable/component routing** enabled by the internal cavity

---

*Note: This summary is intended as a technical description. If you are preparing a patent application, I recommend consulting a registered patent attorney or agent to ensure proper claim drafting and prior-art review.*

# TWO-WHEELER FRAME WITH DIVIDED SUPPORT BRACE CONFIGURATION

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

**[0001]** The present invention relates to a frame structure for a two-wheeler, and more particularly to a frame (10) having a separating surface (20) that traverses through both a left support brace (30) and a right support brace (32) which together hold a rear wheel (40) in position.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

**[0002]** Conventional two-wheeler frames are typically constructed as unitary welded assemblies or employ separating planes that do not coincide with the structural members supporting the rear wheel. Such configurations may present limitations with respect to manufacturability, modularity of assembly, and serviceability of the rear wheel mounting components.

**[0003]** There exists a need for a frame configuration wherein the separating surface is advantageously routed through the support braces to facilitate improved assembly, disassembly, and maintenance of the rear wheel components.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

**[0004]** According to the present invention, there is provided a two-wheeler frame (10) comprising a first frame portion (12) and a second frame portion (14) that are joined at a separating surface (20). The frame (10) includes a left support brace (30) and a right support brace (32) arranged to rotatably receive and hold a rear wheel (40) about a wheel axis (42).

**[0005]** A principal feature of the invention resides in that the separating surface (20) passes through both the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32), such that each said support brace is divided into a first brace segment (34) associated with the first frame portion (12) and a second brace segment (36) associated with the second frame portion (14).

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

**[0006]** Referring to the accompanying description, the two-wheeler frame (10) comprises a first frame portion (12) and a second frame portion (14). The first frame portion (12) and the second frame portion (14) meet along a separating surface (20), which in a preferred embodiment defines a substantially planar interface, though a non-planar contour may equally be employed within the scope of the invention.

**[0007]** The frame (10) further comprises a left support brace (30) and a right support brace (32), the said braces extending rearwardly of the frame (10) and being mutually spaced apart to define a receiving region therebetween for accommodating a rear wheel (40). The rear wheel (40) is rotatably mounted about a wheel axis (42) extending transversely between the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32).

**[0008]** In accordance with the invention, the separating surface (20) is configured such that it passes through both the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32). Accordingly, the left support brace (30) comprises a first brace segment (34) integrally formed with or fixedly attached to the first frame portion (12), and a corresponding second brace segment (36) integrally formed with or fixedly attached to the second frame portion (14). In like manner, the right support brace (32) comprises a first brace segment (34') associated with the first frame portion (12) and a second brace segment (36') associated with the second frame portion (14).

**[0009]** When the first frame portion (12) and the second frame portion (14) are brought together, the respective first and second brace segments (34, 36; 34', 36') of each support brace are placed in abutting engagement across the separating surface (20), thereby reconstituting each of the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32) as a load-bearing member capable of holding the rear wheel (40).

**[0010]** In a preferred embodiment, the separating surface (20) intersects each support brace (30, 32) at a location adjacent the wheel axis (42), such that the wheel axis (42) may be received within or proximate to the separating surface (20). This arrangement permits the rear wheel (40) to be introduced into or removed from the receiving region upon separation of the first frame portion (12) from the second frame portion (14).

**[0011]** Joining means (50) may be provided at the separating surface (20) to releasably secure the first frame portion (12) to the second frame portion (14). The joining means (50) may comprise threaded fasteners, clamping elements, interlocking formations, or equivalent connecting arrangements disposed at or adjacent the first and second brace segments (34, 36; 34', 36').

**[0012]** In an alternative embodiment, the separating surface (20) passes through the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32) along a common plane that is substantially parallel to the wheel axis (42), whereby symmetrical division of both support braces is achieved.

**[0013]** By virtue of the foregoing configuration, the two-wheeler frame (10) affords enhanced modularity, as the first frame portion (12) and the second frame portion (14) may be manufactured separately and thereafter joined at the separating surface (20). Furthermore, servicing of the rear wheel (40) is facilitated, since separation along the separating surface (20) simultaneously opens both the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32).

## CLAIMS

**1.** A two-wheeler frame (10) comprising a first frame portion (12) and a second frame portion (14) joined at a separating surface (20), and a left support brace (30) and a right support brace (32) arranged to hold a rear wheel (40), characterised in that the separating surface (20) passes through both the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32).

**2.** The two-wheeler frame (10) according to claim 1, wherein each of the left support brace (30) and the right support brace (32) is divided by the separating surface (20) into a first brace segment (34, 34') associated with the first frame portion (12) and a second brace segment (36, 36') associated with the second frame portion (14).

**3.** The two-wheeler frame (10) according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the separating surface (20) intersects each support brace (30, 32) adjacent a wheel axis (42) of the rear wheel (40).

**4.** The two-wheeler frame (10) according to any preceding claim, further comprising joining means (50) for releasably securing the first frame portion (12) to the second frame portion (14) at the separating surface (20).

**5.** The two-wheeler frame (10) according to any preceding claim, wherein the separating surface (20) is substantially planar and extends substantially parallel to a wheel axis (42) of the rear wheel (40).

---

## REFERENCE NUMERALS

| Numeral | Component |
|---------|-----------|
| 10 | Two-wheeler frame |
| 12 | First frame portion |
| 14 | Second frame portion |
| 20 | Separating surface |
| 30 | Left support brace |
| 32 | Right support brace |
| 34, 34' | First brace segment |
| 36, 36' | Second brace segment |
| 40 | Rear wheel |
| 42 | Wheel axis |
| 50 | Joining means |
